message.reasoning:
I am playing as player p2 (grok-4.7) in this Monopoly turn.

I paid $28 rent to p1 and now have $54. I need INDIANA_AVENUE to complete the red monopoly. The light blue set is fully owned by p1.

I am checking the remaining properties. p3 owns the dark blue set with 2-3 houses. p4 owns the pink set with 3 houses each and several mortgaged spaces. p1 owns the orange set including Tennessee. The green, yellow, and utilities are mostly mortgaged.

I cannot afford Indiana, and p1 has the light blue hotels. p3 is in jail with $41, while p4 has $407 but mortgaged most of his holdings. My strategy forbids trading reds or mortgaging unless paying a debt, so I have no clear path forward.

Mortgaging both red properties would raise $230, giving me $284 total cash. I am now calculating rent values for the remaining sets to assess immediate threats.

The green set is not a monopoly because Pacific and North Carolina are mortgaged. Indiana would cost about $450 to build three houses on, which I cannot afford.

I cannot build Indiana even if I obtained it for free. Trading my reds to p4 would not help them complete a set, and giving them to p1 would complete p1's red monopoly.
